body.statement: For design A, \(|\mathcal T_A(p,m)|=1\) if and only if the finite observable rank/support/cycle conditions returned by \(\mathscr A(T,m)\) hold. For design B, \(|\mathcal T_B(p)|=1\) if and only if the corresponding residual-forest and cycle conditions returned by \(\mathscr A(T)\) hold. For an arbitrary real input \(\zeta\), every rigid output is either a rational expression in \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\) or a uniquely ordered real element of a finite algebraic extension, certified by a square-free polynomial in \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}[q]\) and Thom sign data. If \(\zeta\) is explicitly rational, this certificate may instead be normalized to a square-free integer polynomial and rational isolating interval. Every nonrigid output contains two legal full SCMs with identical observables and supplied margins, when supplied, but different \(\tau\); both SCMs are strictly positive whenever the nonrigid stratum is interior.
body.justification: This is the necessary-and-sufficient theorem-level kernel and gives an exact coefficient-field meaning to every atlas output.
body.gap: Published proxy results give sufficient full-rank formulas, while published factorization results target nuisance uniqueness rather than PN/PS constancy.
body.consumer: Analysts receive a definitive identification certificate or an explicit observational-equivalence refutation for any fixed finite selected table.

obligation.what_is_open: Necessity and sufficiency of the proposed finite structural atlas on every mixed-support design-A and design-B fiber.
obligation.obstruction: The result requires exhaustiveness of the mixed-support elimination in the sibling-owned open-ended question. The established all-rank-two orientation boxes and conditional residual-forest reduction do not show that inactive rows, coincident endpoints, forced zeros, and all real algebraic support-face components are exhausted. Generic two-copy quantifier elimination would decide constancy but would not prove the claimed structural classifier.
obligation.attempted: Extended the established cycle-to-SCM image equality, all-rank-two orientation classification, and residual-margin forest elimination to every branch they cover, and checked where their arguments stop at rank-one and inactive-row degeneracies.
obligation.partial_result:
By the established cycle-to-SCM lift, the two full-SCM target images are exactly
\[
\mathcal T_A(p,m)
=\{\tau_C(b,a):(b,a)\in\mathcal C_A(T)\},
\qquad
\mathcal T_B(p)
=\{\tau_C(b,a):(b,a,m,g,\pi)\in\mathcal C_B(T)\}.
\]
Consequently, constancy of \(\tau\) on either full fiber is equivalent to constancy of \(\tau_C\) on the corresponding cycle fiber.  If two cycle points have different \(\tau_C\)-values, their lifts are legal full SCMs with the same observables and, in design A, the same supplied margins; the lift permits boundary mechanisms, while an interior cycle pair gives strictly positive twins.  On the all-rank-two design-A branch, the established orientation theorem enumerates at most \(2^4\) closed endpoint boxes and gives a necessary-and-sufficient within-box and cross-box target-agreement test.  For design B, the established residual-forest theorem eliminates the positive unknown margins conditional on \((b,a,\rho)\): at every response type the two incident residuals either both vanish or are nonzero and negatively proportional, active links propagate positive margin ratios, every active cycle has product one, component scales satisfy normalization, and the relevance inequality is then checked.  Thus the claimed rigidity and legal-twin conclusions hold on these completed branches.  What is not derived is exhaustion of all mixed-rank, inactive-row, coincident-endpoint, and forced-zero support faces by the proposed structural chart list.
